reviewNotes: Handoff (SBAR), order tiers, intervention mappings, and event vitals are proposed — not in the original case.
Case gives no vitals for the 0900 change; pain 8/10 is the only scripted change.
source: Instructor case: The Busy Med-Surg Shift — Patient 2
priorityLabel: Moderate priority – pain and mobility management
admittingDx: Osteoarthritis, status post right total knee arthroplasty
hpi: Margaret underwent a right total knee replacement yesterday morning due to severe osteoarthritis. Her postoperative course has been uncomplicated so far. She reports pain at the surgical site, especially with movement. She has been able to ambulate short distances with physical therapy and a walker. Her medical history includes hypertension, hypothyroidism, and osteoarthritis.

handoff.background: HTN, hypothyroidism, OA, obesity. Sulfa allergy. Full code.
handoff.assessment: Pain 6/10 with movement, 3/10 at rest. Dressing intact, minimal drainage. NV intact. Ambulating short distances with walker and PT.
handoff.recommendation: Pain control before PT. NV checks q4h. Enoxaparin due today. Fall precautions.

baseline: Surgical dressing intact with minimal expected postoperative drainage
Right knee with expected postoperative swelling
No signs of acute respiratory distress

findings: States she does not want to get out of bed because it hurts too much

orders.text: Neurovascular checks to right lower extremity every 4 hours
Assess surgical dressing every shift and as needed
Ambulate with walker and one-person assistance
Weight bearing as tolerated to right lower extremity
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO every 6 hours as needed for mild pain
Oxycodone 5 mg PO every 4 hours as needed for moderate to severe pain
Enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneous daily for DVT prophylaxis, subject to bleeding risk and renal function assessment
Apply ice to operative knee as needed
Incentive spirometry every hour while awake
Notify provider for increased bleeding, changes in neurovascular status, uncontrolled pain, or signs of DVT

payload.message: Margaret is requesting pain medication. Reports pain 8/10 and says she doesn't want to get out of bed because it hurts too much.

shouldRecognize: Pain needs to be assessed and treated before mobility.
Medication selection should account for pain severity, sedation, respiratory status, allergies, and prior medication administration.
Reassessment after pain medication is necessary.
Mobility and fall precautions remain important.
Students should assess for complications rather than assuming all postoperative swelling and pain are expected.
